conviction_note: The one thing genuinely absent from every preview in the wire is that this is a 98-day (14-week) quarter against a 91-day (13-week) comp, so MiniMed's own reported and 'organic' growth headlines will print roughly double last quarter's 8.7% for purely calendar reasons; that optic outweighs the softer second-order items (FX cushion gone, Italian-payback flattery in the Q4 base, US Flex/Instinct timing) in a one-session, headline-driven reaction on a 28m-share float, so a small positive.

findings.finding: MiniMed's fiscal Q1 FY27 is a 98-day (14-week) quarter — 2026-04-25 through 2026-07-31 — against a 91-day (13-week) prior-year quarter (2025-04-26 through 2025-07-25); the entire 53rd week of FY27 falls in this single quarter, and MiniMed's own definition of 'Organic Revenue Growth' adjusts only for FX and Italian payback accruals, NOT for extra weeks, so the organic-growth headline will print roughly double the 8.7% it printed for Q4 FY26 on calendar alone. The dates are established by the company's own filings: FY26 ended 2026-04-24 (Q4 exhibit 99.1), the year-ago quarter ended 2025-07-25 (Medtronic 10-Q mdt-20250725), and this quarter ends 2026-07-31 (the 2026-07-20 announcement).
findings.why_not_priced: Management pre-guided the arithmetic on the 3 June call, so the five covering analysts almost certainly have it in the $828.43m consensus — but the pre-print wire copy does not. The 26 August previews (Benzinga, scanx) carry only '$0.09 vs $0.35 EPS' and '$828.43m revenue' and explicitly do not mention the extra week, FX, or the split-off. If the marginal holder had internalised that Q1 organic growth is mechanically ~15% rather than ~9%, you would expect a visible pre-print run-up rather than 20d +4.55% / 5d +0.15% at exactly the $20 IPO price, and you would not see two of five analysts (BofA $27->$20 on 18 May, Wells $26->$22 on 4 June) cutting targets into it. The first session is priced off the release headline, and the only prior print — a GAAP loss of $(0.68) that still produced +15.93% — is direct evidence this name trades off the growth line, not the EPS line.
findings.independence: Corroborated independently by Medtronic's own FY27 guidance shape: Q1 FY27 non-GAAP EPS guided $1.38-1.40 (+~10% on Q1 FY26's $1.26) versus full-year growth of ~7%, which only reconciles if the 53rd week sits in Q1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1613103/000162828026040034/exhibit991-fy26q4earningsr.htm). Year-ago quarter-end date independently from the Medtronic Q1 FY26 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1613103/000161310325000161/mdt-20250725.htm

findings.finding: The euro tailwind that supplied roughly half of Q4 FY26's reported-vs-organic gap (15.6% reported vs 8.7% organic) is gone in this quarter: EURUSD monthly averages for May/Jun/Jul 2026 were 1.1681/1.1510/1.1419 (avg 1.1536) versus 1.1276/1.1518/1.1698 a year earlier (avg 1.1497) — +0.34% y/y, against +8.2% y/y for the Feb-Apr window that Q4 FY26 covered. MiniMed's 10-K puts OUS revenue at ~70% of FY26 total (Q4 FY26: international $599m of $837m, US only $238m), making it one of the most FX-levered US-listed medtechs.
findings.why_not_priced: FX is the single most-modelled line on the sell side, so I size this small — most of it is in the $828m number. What is not priced is the interaction: the market's mental model of MMED is 'US insulin pump company with a new US pump', and a 70%-OUS revenue base whose reported growth has been running 7 points above organic on currency is not how a name trading at its IPO price with 833 contracts of total option open interest is being held. If it were understood, the reported-growth deceleration from a 7pt FX cushion to zero would have shown up as a pre-print de-rating rather than a 20d gain.
findings.independence: Prior-year rates from the same publisher's 2025 page (https://www.x-rates.com/average/?from=EUR&to=USD&amount=1&year=2025); the 70% OUS figure is from a different document, MiniMed's FY26 10-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002062583/000162828026045915/mdt-20260424.htm

findings.finding: About $20m of Q4 FY26's $837m reported revenue was not product demand: the 'Other' line jumped to $22m from $2m a year earlier and the footnote defines it as 'net sales generated from the sales of smart insulin pens and services. Amounts in this line also reflect adjustments to the Company's Italian payback accruals' — a legal-accrual release that is expressly excluded from the organic growth definition. Anyone extrapolating the $837m base into Q1 has carried a one-off forward, and the underlying Italian exposure is live rather than settled: the Council of State (Ordinance No. 1589/2026) suspended industry appeals against the Ministry of Health decree of 29 December 2023 and referred the Medical Device Governance Fund to the Italian Constitutional Court.
findings.why_not_priced: This is a footnote to a supplementary revenue table in a press-release exhibit, not a headline item; no preview, initiation note summary or wire story I could find mentions the Italian payback at all. If it were priced, a $20m swing factor on a $830m quarter — 2.4 points of reported growth, sitting outside the organic definition and therefore invisible to anyone anchoring on 'organic' — would appear in preview commentary as a bridge item, and it does not. The sign is genuinely two-sided, which is why the band straddles zero.
findings.independence: The Italian litigation status is from an entirely separate source chain: https://www.jdsupra.com/legalnews/a-new-tax-on-medical-device-3576983/ (Hogan Lovells, on Council of State Ordinance No. 1589/2026 referring the Medical Device Governance Fund to the Constitutional Court)

findings.finding: The US business — the whole basis of the Flex equity story — grew 1.5% in Q4 FY26 ($238m of $837m) versus +12.2% organic internationally, and the reporting quarter cannot show the Flex inflection because Flex's actual differentiator arrived after quarter end: MiniMed's 2026-08-17 release says Flex 'now shipping' with Abbott's 15-day Instinct sensor, 17 days after the 2026-07-31 close, while the 2026-06-17 US launch release told customers the Instinct pairing was investigational and 'expected later in summer 2026'. The company therefore told prospective US pump buyers, inside the quarter, that a materially better bundle was weeks away.
findings.why_not_priced: Coverage treats the 17 June US launch and the 17 August Instinct availability as two positive product headlines; nobody has joined them into 'the six weeks of Flex that land in this quarter were sold against a publicly pre-announced upgrade seventeen days out'. If the market had done that arithmetic, the 17 August release would have read as a mild negative revision to the reported quarter rather than as good news, and Flex-driven price targets would not still sit $20-26 against a $19.97 spot. The offset — and the reason this is only worth a point or so — is that the same fact makes Q2 commentary easy for management to spin.
findings.independence: The 1.5% US growth and $238m US figure come from a different document, the Q4 FY26 earnings exhibit 99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2062583/000162828026040036/exhibit991-fy26q4earningsr.htm); the 'expected later in summer 2026' language is in the 2026-06-17 launch release, https://news.minimed.com/2026-06-17-MiniMeds-Smallest-App-Controlled-Insulin-Pump-is-Now-Available-in-the-U-S

findings.finding: Medtronic's April 2026 intrusion (ShinyHunters, unauthorised access 13-19 April 2026) resulted in notification of 3,834,294 individuals, with letters going out from late June into July 2026 — squarely inside MiniMed's fiscal Q1 — and several class actions already filed; exposed fields include Social Security numbers and health information. MiniMed filed its own Reg-FD 8-K on the incident on 2026-04-27 saying it was 'not aware of any compromises to the IT systems used by its business', but it has never quantified exposure, and the Q1 10-Q is the first periodic filing that must address it while MiniMed still runs on Medtronic IT under the separation arrangements.
findings.why_not_priced: The breach is universally covered as a Medtronic story and was priced (to the extent it was priced at all) into MDT in late April; the diabetes business is the one Medtronic unit with millions of direct patient records (pumps, sensors, supply reordering), so MiniMed's share of the 3.8m is plausibly large, yet no MMED-specific coverage exists and MMED sits 3.5% off its 52-week high. If the market had attributed a material share of the remediation, indemnity and litigation exposure to MMED, you would see it in the pre-print tape and in a discount to the $20 IPO price, not a 20d gain.
findings.independence: MiniMed's own Reg-FD 8-K on the incident, a separate primary source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2062583/000110465926049045/tm2612783d1_8k.htm

findings.finding: Informative absence on the largest feared mechanical event: as of 2026-08-31 neither Medtronic (CIK 0001613103) nor MiniMed (CIK 0002062583) has filed a Form S-4, Schedule TO or Form 425 for the split-off exchange offer, so an exchange offer cannot legally launch in the days around this print, and Medtronic's FY27 EPS guidance still 'assumes consolidation of the Diabetes business for the full 12 months of FY27'. Separation groundwork is visibly proceeding but at governance pace, not offer pace — the board went from 9 to 11 on 2026-06-29 adding Alcon CEO David Endicott as an independent director, and the first annual meeting is set for 2026-10-09.
findings.why_not_priced: The received framing around any Medtronic carve-out is that the split-off exchange offer, launched at a discount, forces arbitrage shorting of a 28m-share float and caps the subsidiary — and the +22.1 vol-point 25-delta put skew is the kind of print that framing produces. The registration docket says that cannot happen in this window. This is worth little on its own, but it is the reason I do not read the skew as a directional statement, and confirming an absence at zero cost is the point.
findings.independence: The full-12-month consolidation assumption is from a separate document, Medtronic's Q4 FY26 earnings exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1613103/000162828026040034/exhibit991-fy26q4earningsr.htm); the board expansion is from MiniMed's 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2062583/000110465926078588/tm2619270d1_8k.htm

searched_and_found_nothing: Medtronic and MiniMed EDGAR dockets for a split-off Form S-4 / Schedule TO / Form 425 — none exists as of 2026-08-31

IPO lock-up expiry mechanics: no prospectus lock-up release-trigger language or waiver news found; and because Medtronic wants a tax-free split-off rather than a cash sale, the ~180-day mark is not a real supply event for the 90% stake

FDA device recall / early alert database and MedTech Dive recall coverage for any 2026 field action on MiniMed Flex or Simplera Sync — nothing in the reporting quarter; the Simplera Sync sensor supply and reliability complaints on diabetes.co.uk all date from Feb-Oct 2025 and are in the base

App-store telemetry: Google Play would not render download counts or review counts for the Flex controller app (com.minimed.diabetes.instinct.us), and the iOS Flex app is not surfaced in App Store search; the only readable datapoint was the legacy MiniMed Mobile US app at 3.0 stars on 482 ratings with a ~2026-08-26 review reporting iOS 26.6.1 incompatibility — too small and too legacy to size

California WARN notices / hiring-page inflection: the only MiniMed-related action found is the February 2026 notice cutting 81 Northridge roles effective 2026-04-07, which pre-dates the quarter and is already reported
Insider Form 4s: no open-market purchases or sales by MMED officers or directors after the March 2026 IPO-related cluster
MMED short interest as a percentage of the 28m-share float — no dated figure retrievable from any source I could reach; flagged unavailable rather than estimated

Insulet Q2 2026 (23% cc growth, second-highest new customer starts) and the CMS DMEPOS competitive-bidding conversion of pumps and CGM to monthly rental — both real but sector-level, in the wire, and with an effective date of 2028
The 2026-08-05 8-K: General Counsel Courtney Nelson Wills resigning effective 2026-09-25 for personal reasons — checked, judged cosmetic, not sized

Any leading disclosure from Medtronic's simultaneous release: MDT reports the same quarter at the same minute (5:45 a.m. CT = 3:45 a.m. PDT on 2026-09-01), so there is no informational lead to exploit
baseline_tension: My main finding cuts directly against the baseline's priced lean: the +22.1 vol-point 25-delta put skew and 4.59 put/call open-interest ratio say downside is being paid, while the mechanics say the growth headline gets a one-off calendar boost — and I treat that skew as unusable anyway, since it rests on 833 total contracts with an ATM spread at 174% of mid, so it is quote noise rather than a statement; the flat 5-day tape at exactly the $20 IPO price is consistent with nobody having positioned for either the 14-week quarter or the FX cushion disappearing, and my net number (+2.0) is far inside the baseline's 15.93% single-observation expected move because a six-month-old carve-out with five analysts can move three times that on anything.
